--- title: "The exercise" subtitle: "Short" bibliography: [../../references.bib, ../../references-new.bib] --- The [background page](../../background.qmd) presents the original study, the SCORE replication and the five reanalyses of the robustness study of SCORE [Multi100\; @AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]. The short format takes Tasks 1 to 4, and you do them in the deck of the session, whose slides run R inside your browser with the data already in place. The [browser lab](../../lab.qmd) holds the same tasks and is the fallback if the deck does not load. --- ## The claim Five independent analysts reanalysed one claim of the original authors (OAs) [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect] in the robustness study. The claim, as the analysts received it, was: > "Hispanic housing applicants were ... less likely to be greeted by name than were ... white counterparts" (p. 100 of the published article) The published result behind it is the coefficient of the Hispanic names in a logistic regression of a named greeting on the three groups of names, with community controls and the Hard Email indicator: **−0.82 (standard error 0.22) on 549 replies**, which the OAs translate into a gap of **−20.0 percentage points** in the probability of a named greeting, with a 95% confidence interval from −30.5 to −10.0. The data come from an experiment: 1,014 emails to housing authorities, each of which was signed with one of six names that were assigned at random. ## The five analysts {#the-five-analysts} ::: {#tbl-five .cell tbl-cap='The five reanalyses, with the statistic recorded in the robustness study and the gap in percentage points by the course refit. Source: `data/analysts5.csv`.'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
Analyst Comparison Emails counted Recorded statistic Gap (points) Conclusion in Task 1
8PTRZ Hispanic against other names replies χ2 = 14.265 −17.3 evidence for the claim
UYV3F Hispanic against white names replies z = −3.771 −20.0 evidence for the claim
EWFMI Hispanic against white names (three-group model) replies z = 3.645 −19.4 evidence for the claim
25N5D Hispanic against white names all delivered emails χ2 = 13.683 −13.2 no evidence either way
P9W8Y three groups replies none recorded −20.0 no evidence either way
``` ::: ::: All five found Hispanic names greeted by name less often than the comparison names, and all four recorded statistics reproduce exactly on the public file. Two of the five nevertheless concluded in Task 1 of the robustness study that the data showed no evidence either way, and the [background page](../../background.qmd#sec-reanalysts) sets out what question each analyst answered. --- ## The tasks The session takes four of the five numbered tasks of the exercise, in the cells of its deck. ### Task 1 – The setup check Wait for the engine of the deck to finish downloading, then run the setup cell. ### Task 2 – The estimand statement Write the **estimand statement** behind the claim, in the chat. It says which comparison is made (Hispanic names against which names), which emails are counted (the replies, or every delivered email), and which outcome is compared. The [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) gives the template. ### Task 3 – The reproduction Choose one of the five analysts in the table above and reproduce the analysis from the public file of the OAs, `housing_original.csv` ([codebook](../../data/housing_original_codebook.md)), in the cells of that analyst. Then find out why your number is what it is. A reproduction depends on the defaults and the codings of the software as well as on the data and the model. ### Task 4 – The menu This task is **exploratory**: nothing in it is preregistered, and you may look, change your mind and try again. Try several specifications from the [specification menu](../../menu.qmd) with `try_spec()`, one decision at a time, and note which choices move the estimate and which barely touch it. Then choose the one that you would defend and run it once more, so that it is your last try, because the slides place it among the 64 specifications of the curve. The session sends nothing to the class chart. ### Task 5 – Declaration and report The session stops before this task, in which you choose **one** specification and complete a preregistration block before you run it, and before the class chart. The page [After the session](after.qmd) says where to take both up. --- ## What counts as a result The session sends nothing to the class chart, and the rule below applies to the results that you send later. A result counts for the class chart if it is one of the 64 specifications on the curve, if it reaches the chart through `submit_exploration()` or `report_result()`, which fill in the class-results form for you, and if it comes with a written reason for each choice; two sentences are enough. The reasons are what make a set of different results more than a spread of numbers, because they show which differences between results come from different questions and which from different ways of answering the same one. --- ## Links The tools of the session: - [Slides](slides.qmd) - [Browser lab](../../lab.qmd) The pages of the case study: - [Background](../../background.qmd) - [Specification menu](../../menu.qmd) - [Decision map](../../menu.qmd#map) - [Specification curve](../../curve.qmd) - [Class results](../../class-results.qmd)
